My NFT Artwork — SPIRIT ANIMAL

![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/d2f9f1b0-02f5-4172-937b-8cbd38b8a874/20250912-1600x900-SPIRITANIMAL-by-dougfriesen.jpg)


So this was a challenge while on one of my walks in Quebec City. My time was spent in a concrete jungle that does not lean itself into nature nor wildlife. But that was not going to stop me from trying. I was reminded of a simple yet powerful statement from my young son (it is pasted on the wall in their classroom):

---------------------

Mistakes are just proof you are trying.

---------------------

Attempt after attempt I could find the right inspiration to match it up in these travels. So, I decided to just pack up my gear into the backpack and go for a long walk to the lower section, exploring some of the local culture. On the path there, a small back alley is the conduit to the main pedestrian area. It is populated with street artists that have unique enclosure displays built into the exterior walls within. This is where I ran into this horse. A lonely mural. It caught my attention. The horse as if in reverence to the onlooker. There was peace. The art and the art spoke to each other in ways only love knows. Was this my spirit animal? Was this my sign to stop?


I grabbed my gear and tried to frame the shot in between passerby's. The artwork and the horse spoke to each other. There was common ground. Success.


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/dd618b5a-e1aa-4937-b120-ce93ee55bf73/20260417-0316-zr-2400x1600-quebec-city-by-dougfriesen.jpg)


I broke down the inspiration and components (layers and blend modes utilizing primarily traditional photography as source) I used to create this artwork on my website.


Never give up. Never stop loving.  Re-discover your art outside. You will be blessed.


The Art of Spirit Animal.

**EVERYTHING MUST GO** 

![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/357283b3-dfc9-4e76-9e1c-acbc5606ff30/20250518-1800x1800-everythingmustgo-by-dougfriesen.jpg)

from my Bitcoin Ordinal created collection


I know I have shared this ordinal before, BUT when I was in Quebec City, I searched several times looking for context and frame. This was from one of the other outings I embarked on that I have not shown. 


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/29b414eb-9639-4e2e-bd86-3b32711a05ab/20260417-0360-zr-quebec-city-by-dougfriesen-bw-w.jpg)


In this context, I used the juxtaposition of the art to the background where:

(1) The cars parked are all to the left direction, yet the car in the art is to the right. Simply this is because the artwork was captured in London and the context in Canada. But it also spoke to the reversing of direction. Everything that goes up must come down within the reach of gravity. 

(2) I saw modern trendy stores across the road as I walked. Luxury cars lined the street. It was a stark contrast to the original art captured where a classic automobile was parked, living its end of life, in front of stores that had already reached irrelevance. Everything must go. Last day. 

(3) I presented the final frame in black and white as it complemented the monochrome photographic art well.


It cements the value of time. It speaks to the value of experiences and memories vs possessions. Everything must submit to entropy. And when it does, all we have left are memories. This is why photography is so important to me. It captures moments in time, forever encapsulating them into pixels to live on. For in the end, we just have each other.


Live with kindness every day. 🤍

Gm Gm OUTSIDERS 🤍

I am back for another instalment of taking and enjoying minted art in the real world.

The sun was finally shining again today. It wasn't warm, thus the gloves (edit: -10c), but there is beauty in this brown season. And much like how the colours pop in my Ordinal NFT — TRANSMIT, which is listed on Gamma. The colour really jumped out today in the mute season that is neither winter nor spring. The sky is still this beautiful gentle blue. The fields, strewn of last harvest, are now clear of snow, and this perfect light brown/beige. It complements the sky so perfectly in these muted pastel shades. And yes, I have neutral colour gloves specifically so that they do not detract from an image if they are part of it. 

It would be a completely zen location, minus that this is a busy stretch of highway. I know there are those curious as they turn heads going by, wondering why I am taking images of my phone along the transmission lines. Yesterday, I delayed my arrival at the easter gathering as I wanted to see if there were opportunities outside as well. I had to explain to my mother-in-law the purpose of it and then 6529 as a result. My kids already understand and tell me I should stop and take some more pictures outside of my art.

Fun fact: The orientation I am standing is correct to the original. The sun really does set to the West (left side of the artwork - which is why it is red/orange going to yellow) and thus the blue sky ends last in the East to match within the art. Every pixel has purpose.

I wanted this minted artwork to represent the zen I feel when I sit under transmission lines as they silently sway, crackle and pop, endure hardships of weather, yet never complain. Each tower alone could not bear the weight, but as a community they share the burden and can withstand anything. Welcome to decentralized culture. Is there a meme submission coming using transmission towers or lines... most certainly there will. It might even team up with my printing/design history.

Gm Gm Outsiders!

Well, I was determined to take another NFT into the outside world today. Spring break for the kids is upon us and I don't know how much time I will get to create during non-dark hours — thus here is a another contribution.... so, we were hosting friends tonight for supper. This allowed for opportunity to grab my shot (as I was on bbq duty) and inspire conversation as to why, and what i was shooting on the NFT on my phone and then how that art was made, when I returned inside. I had not had the opportunity to share that specific visual artwork with him before, so this was a perfect segway to share this art + passion. Wine. Steak ka-bobs. Asparagus. Sautéed Mushrooms. Garlic Bread. Mmm.

The NFT is an Ordinal on Bitcoin. It is titled THE COLLECTOR.

THE PROCESS: This is pure photography. Shot in a winter setting, ice was sitting on the net of the trampoline from a hoar frost style buildup the night before. The final steps were to convert to monochrome and invert the image — a recurring theme in my art. Next, I adjusted the curves to taste. The net used for the NFT is the very same one as show in the background of this art image.

THE RESULT: It felt abstract and organic. I then followed up the art with an official flash fiction embedded into the metadata of the NFT Ordinal. The ice had now been transformed into crushed carbon remains of planets within this honeycomb. The flash fiction brings this art piece to life. I loved the dusk sky to contrast the monochrome art when presenting it here. always art within the art.

THE OFFICIAL FLASH FICTON: Occupying the void outside of time, I survey my work. When I created this universe, there was perfection. But something changed, and I can’t find the error. There is a rotten disease that has infected all that begins. Who am I? I am the God-King. I transcend time. I do not know my origin, except that I am eternal. My creation cannot comprehend my majesty nor show me reverence. With just a mere snap of my fingers I can crush any planet, system, or the entire universe as it is known. The darkness I see cannot be left to flourish. It only brings me more pain. And so I crush planet by planet where life has begun, folding space like a simple piece of paper in order to reach into their ignorant existence and assert my dominion. Their screams are but dust in the wind–of no consequence. To remind me of this rage, I place the remains of each darkened planet, mangled and broken, into my honeycomb. Yet I cannot reconcile what is happening. I love my creation, but hate what they have become. Are they just a reflection? 

“Bobby! Stop daydreaming and play the game!” invades my ear canals… Shocked back to reality, or what I think is reality, I find myself sitting in front of the TV, controller in hand. Logged out of the game, I re-enter my gamer handle: The Collector. The server reloads. A new world begins to burn.

There is a whole book in here somewhere "Adventures of the Freedom Towel".

Amazing to see the love this gets and PLEASE keep bringing it outside!

Another day. Another Artwork.

Today I was contemplating @[fercaggiano]'s recent minted Meme Card, "An Artist's Life".

There were several reasons I loved it. First, the artwork is fabulous. It is playful. It encapsulates passion, pressure and survival. That got me thinking. As an artist/photographer myself, there pressures from all sides economically, passion, and social recognition for fear of falling into the void of the algorithm.

This round trips to 6529 and the absence of algo. The return to being seen for who you are and what you do. And then there was the conversation to took it to collectors, just like artists feel pressure and are tested for passion in journey of survival through market conditions.

It often comes down to one defining characteristic. Do you have passion for art — whether collector or artist? If you do, then the most critical aspect for longevity is secured. There will always be pressure in bull or bear markets. There will always be the fight for survival amongst the many, but passion — the LOVE for what you do, create or collect, it what leads.

And thus, this Meme Card holds a special message for me as well. We are not alone in this journey. And I LOVE what I capture. I LOVE what I create. I LOVE every single interaction that involves art and the positive path forward.  So, here I focused on queuing her artwork here, next to the heart of I LOVE QUEBEC sign at the conference centre. Fitting.

Gm Gm Outsiders!


BREATH OF ANOTHER

An inscribed Ordinal from my Art Exploration collection on Gamma.


With each step the air was becoming more granular—walls closing in. A familiar sensation, Misfiled by the mind. Inscribed on a Black Uncommon Rare Sat (vintage 2016).


Quebec City was the perfect location — enough old world feel to complement the final artwork which has its origins in Cinque Terre from 2016 when the core image within the art was captured. I then inscribed the art onto a Black Uncommon Rare Sat, also of 2016 vintage. The challenge was to give it life outside, where the surroundings would pose as an extension of the work — a frame of sorts.


Entering the old city, one has to walk through a stone fortress wall. The narrow archway was the answer to my search. The concept was to move phone with the art so that it would cover the exit of the tunnel ahead of me. The shadows cast by the sunlight and old materials were perfect as I stood outside the wall. The darkened shadows balance the black background of the inscribed art. The pathway exit to the covered walk within the original art is convenient held in place to mimic the exit through the wall. 


This instance benefited from a full monochrome conversion of this OUTSIDERS art rendition to become one with the art, as the original artwork is also monochrome.


Adventure Does Not Wait.

Gm Gm Outsiders 🤍


Today I bring you a little art appreciation while BBQ'ing.


**COSMIC RINSE** ![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/f846cba9-042d-4728-8db8-4e071e494d6d/20250514-1800x1800-cosmic-rinse-by-dougfriesen.jpg)

This is an NFT Ordinal on Bitcoin created from my photography via layers/blends.


Today's association between the art and the environment is different than my usual view points. I was bbq'ing delicious steak kabobs and asparagus. And as I was taking in the light of the day that would soon fade, I kept being reminded that beautiful light follows sunny days such as it was. The smell of the sizzling food saturated the air around me. Yet I couldn't help to drift to the amount of work it would be to clean up after hosting this event for friends. As a host, I spend my time here preparing and serving, often only eating at the very end when others are done or almost ready for dessert.


It is with this odd connection of thoughts that brought me to exactly what I had created. The burning sunset embedded within does represent the heat of the flame under the grates in front of me. This was created by two unlikely candidates. The first was a sunset at a  nature sanctuary near me (which is not much different than I can see from my back yard). The second is actually from a top down image shot with my iPhone of the soapy sink water that was remaining after a round of dishes following a meal. I added a starfield into the final mix as well, which tied the title almost literally... Cosmic Rinse.


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/5718f18f-6286-49d4-b720-51b67c9fa8d6/20260329-9613-zr-outsiders-dougfriesen-web.jpg)


Art exists everywhere — Our back yards, drives to here and there, beneath our feet, above our heads, and in and out of our hearts. Take a moment to appreciate everything in front of you... even dirty sink water can become art.


And as always, my friends know I will bring out the camera and shoot something, which often has turned to shooting art within the art. A great exercise of the mind to think deeper and see beyond the surface.

Gm Gm Outsiders!


Today I bring a atmosphere from Quebec City while enjoying my illustration art SURRENDER. It is an NFT available on Manifold. 


Upon arriving, rain followed us and was unrelenting every day, save for today when all that was left was a heavy fog over the city. This made the perfect backdrop for framing my art outside. The theme is the same. Unrendered distances/futures/visions.


------------------------

In life, there are unknowns-distances unrendered until they draw near. Yet we carry on with hope, even as days burn and nights descend into darkness.

------------------------


Yes, I fretted over where I would match this artwork IRL. This was perfect. Soft touches of yellows, greens and reds spot the city below to tie into the colour matrix of the art. The intensity of the art clashes with the pastel of the fog reducing contrast behind. The limited viewing distance from the fog reminds us that the future is not always known. What was is not always what is, vice verse. But what remains important is that we keep forging ahead into the unknown with passion and resolve. We can build a better tomorrow. one story. one action. one kind deed. one hello at a time. 


Spread your wings. This is your journey.


For computer nerds of yesteryear, yes this is also a play on that and the limited draw distance when playing so many games. The same philosophy is true.

Gm Gm OUTSIDERS!


It's been a while. Opportunities have been slim, but I had a few moments to pull out my phone and celebrate meme card by @[Hoizon] (Sir, A Needle) when out with a buddy two nights ago. It was quite fitting. So often when we have been out shooting, the scenario of what we saw coming and what became has been very different. Like a rug pull, the scene would simply fizzle when we arrived on location. This week we were searching for a combination of a canola field with dark clouds to the south with an evening sun would light up the field all while waiting for strikes of lightning in that very same dark sky. I know I know, that is a big ask. 


We found what we were looking for — and there were strikes of lightning while setting up. Yes! But alas, the moment we were ready, the last strike for the evening had already occurred much like the clown popping the kid's balloon, and just like that, it was over. 


I should have moved past the transmission pole for composition, but the dark blue background and yellow base of the GIF also complement the IRL sky and landscape as an added bonus. The balloon had already been popped in the GIF much like our opportunity which was gone.

**ZEUS AND TYPHON**

I am back with another instalment of what inspired me in the moment, outside.

This past weekend, I spent an entire day shooting with a buddy from sunrise to sunset. To begin the day, we watched the rising sun from a local lake. Unfortunately the mid and high clouds cleared out and left nothing in the sky to amplify the moments of twilight before the sun broke the horizon. With the clouds, it would have lit up in brilliant colours. The sunrise was still beautiful, but the bar is high for what I was aiming for. At this very same time, it came to me that I could use the sunrise that were we given for a brilliant pair up with a Meme Card. The recent art by @[Minotaur_Man] was so good and fit the moment. He has some amazing art. Check his profile out.

In this twilight, the colours of the Meme Card and nature were harmonious. The location was also on point for the fact that this was a water based scene. I tried to place it in the scene so that it would fit compositionally. The waterfall pouring in from the top left also comes as a bright strength to the main subject, much like the brightness from the rising sun that was en route from the upper left in the lake scene. Even the colours from the card are somewhat mimic'd in the lake and sky creating a "meant to be" vibe.

Why is my arm and hand completely crushed into shadows intentionally to give more prominence to the Meme Card art that was on my phone and the landscape before me. **COSMIC RINSE**

Today, I present one of my nft inscriptions that I have shown before, but in a completely different context. A buddy and I had just arrived in the small Saskatchewan community of Moosomin. It sits on the Trans-Canada Highway. 

Before I dwelve into the art, I just want to say that if you ever happen to find yourself driving by, stop at The Red Barn. The food is amazing.

We were there for their annual fireworks competition. Touring fireworks companies take turns each night showing off their choreographed skills while they light up the night. It takes place at the lake, a few miles out of town. This allows them to showcase bigger fireworks. 

We spent a total of 7 hours driving and a night at the hotel for a mere 16 minutes. Crazy. But this is life. We live for moments, anticipate events, and remember times good and bad. Some feel like forever while others are fleeting.

While we waited on the darkened beach, the last light was leaving and I felt this nft was the perfect compliment. A marriage between dark nature and human created light, much like my artwork which merges dirty sink water with soap and the nature of a sunset and stars.

But wait, that's not all. We often overlook the inclusion of ourselves and those we experience events with as photographers. So this second one is a perfect context to the evening. I created art with my photography for the original **COSMIC RINSE** and then captured it in the real world on the beach while waiting for the night sky to light up all while my buddy was capturing the distant shore as we were planning our night of shooting... cameras were on tripods and lawn chairs were ready. 

Thus this picture encapsulates the complete cycle of creative live... capture, create, showcase, capture, repeat.


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/950d98b0-f501-4a63-9cf3-8edb7e15302a/20260802-2-a7r6-moosomin-by-dougfriesen-w.png)


This is the actual NFT that I created from that sink water, a glorious sunset and some star shine. No AI. Just human touch.

May your nights burn bright with creative spirit. Art is culture.

Originally, I had intended to do this challenge on Sunday at a different location. However, as my daughter broke her arm on the weekend and my son was having a tough weekend, there was no opportunity to head out. I was disappointed. But, I was not going to let that define my participation. I had some extra time today, so this was my priority. I do also enjoy taking my art out and re-discovering it and the details. It was inconvenient as it is 26x40 inches and only myself this time. So I grabbed a display stand, canvas, and my camera. The canvas sits on the wall in our entrance to greet guests.


Ready to go shoot...

![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/b0182fd8-a701-4b7d-b376-752031c0d9d2/IMG-4581-rockstar-by-dougfriesen-w.jpg) 

The location from Sunday was not an option, so I took a drive to a nearby walking path which was void of the rich flowers it usually is adorned with. But, the white skies at the time didn't do anything for the aesthetics. Though it still became the location that I took advantage of for the art on the phone capture outside. So this is kinda two posts in one.


Location Scouting #1

![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/bb575699-1efa-4786-80eb-e3fd56c097d9/20260506-1006-z8-OUTSIDERS-Rockstar-dougfriesen-PL9-w.jpg) 

This worked well with the digital version. The contrast of pure colour against a background that was still void of life, save for grass that was more than just winter brown. The curvy path mimics the stamen. The reflection of the trees on the phone make it feel like they are reaching upwards to that light above the canopy. And I am in there, kinda. But, this was not the place for the canvas.


Walking back to the car I found Location #2

![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/781f01da-a909-4ead-869e-ac688a93ae1c/20260506-1013-z8-OUTSIDERS-Rockstar-dougfriesen-PL9-w.jpg) 

Oooh. I kinda loved this spot. Literally on the sidewalk beside the road. Not a place I could shoot the canvas, but also perfect for the phone and the juxtaposition of the background to art in colour vs monochromatic made it jump off the screen. Even my arm blends in. The watch band oddly helps balance yet complements the blues in the art. I was happy with this....


But the canvas. The title is ROCKSTAR. So I had an idea. What if I took it to the local outdoor performance stage? It is where concerts happen. So off I went... Now I did underestimate the wind and had the canvas with tripod blow OFF the stage on the ground twice. Very inconvenient. Fortunately it did not damage. These are amazing canvases.


Onstage.

Taking art OUTSIDE is what we all need to do.

Your future self will thank you.

My NFT Artwork — GOODBYE HELLO SUN

![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/8758cd01-c519-4112-b3ed-1cdc34431d77/202501003-1200x1800-hellogoodbyesun-by-dougfriesen.jpg)


It's actually kinda fitting. This was one of my last walks out when I was in Quebec City. The week had been full of rain and this was particularly is BRIGHT sunny day and yet it was time to say goodbye to a place i adore and peace of quietly walking the streets and capturing some art of what is along the way.


When I originally created this piece, the following was and is the descriptor for it:

-------------------------

A roar shudders the ground beneath my feet. The storm has left its weight behind, flooding the earth in torrents that claw at the void. Darkness presses in with a violence that deafens.

I stagger toward the horizon. The sun burns low, yet its warmth is being devoured. Fractured and torn, the sky breaks into sharpened shapes—testing my grasp on what remains of order, shadows above continue to crush the air from this place. The urge to escape coils tight.

Peace slips away, not stolen but dissolved, leaving me caged within a mind that no longer trusts its own. A day like any other has become a battleground.

-------------------------


Yet as I was walking, it became an emotional connection that was filled with longing to stay in this brief moment in time. Making my way down Rue Saint-Jean, I again had nothing that connected. I put away my camera and began looking for somewhere to grab a snack and refreshment. It was at that time that I walked past a side street which took me on a journey to 41 Rue Charlevoix, home of "Le Monastère des Augustines - Hôtel bien-être". A fascinating place I did not know about and would love to stay at next time I am there. 


And then I saw my inspiration. It wasn't grand. It wasn't nature. But like nature and the cycle of our days as we revolve around our sun, it is essential. A fire hydrant. Quiet. Stoic. Standing without fanfare or complaint in the hot sun. It was bright yellow/red/blue. This triggered the idea that it would make a perfect companion to my NFT. Attempting to capture the moment was more difficult as it is a darker piece and the sun was intense, but as I was doing that, I noticed my own shadow of me capturing this very moment. To my left is that Monastery.  


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/4c31254a-a185-4b60-a864-2f46153a5c24/20260417-0231-zr-quebec-city-by-dougfriesen-w.jpg)


Hello. Goodbye. Sun. We will meet again. I'll bring the camera. You bring the culture.

My NFT Artwork: THE WISHING TREE

![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/ccbf7ca8-5607-475d-8bb4-1efd0e79e3b8/20160527-1800x1200-thewishingtree-by-dougfriesen.jpg)


Outsiders Location #1: Walking back to the hotel along Rue Saint-Jean in Quebec City, I found this old public telephone box. The years have aged it with graffiti and stickers. Yet, this disrepair become my focus. The juxtaposition between foreground and background was the interconnectedness of the tree and it's branches much like people and communities. The box has aged and passed its prime. Paint peeling. Stickers cover its being. The tree, void of leaves and life, faces another season of change. The stickers represent all the community of passerby's — some to read and others to engage and propagate. We are all connected in this chaos.


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/a429853a-2bb6-4e95-8cf0-f7764c57c331/20260417-0405-zr-quebecity-by-dougfriesen-w.jpg)


Outsiders Location #2: Manitoba. My buddy Steve and I had just returned from an all day seminar listening to inspiration and story from an amazing Canadian Photographer, Curtis Jones. After arriving back in our community, we prepped to go out to shoot sunset. The clouds that had teased us with potential colour were no where to be found. But blue skies at sunset do make great silhouettes as well. First, the Outsiders....


First take away is how different art can be interpreted. Life experiences, location, colour, time, content, all play important factors to our perspectives and the message.


What was exceptionally busy in composition background at the first location was now given space to breathe. Second take away is with less content, the depth can grow. This is also true of possessions. Often less is more. We gain more appreciation for what we do have.


We were standing on the front lawn of a funeral home which was to the left with the setting sun to the right, leaving two barren trees in the center (we know the director, thus it wasn't trespassing — respect is important in photography). I probably should have placed my phone in the location of one of the trees to mimic it's place in the the scene, but I didn't. I should have shot wider to give better perspective of the building in contrast to the nature, but I didn't. Perfectly imperfect. It represents the circle of life, like the seasons of nature. The funeral home is a reminder that all things fall to entropy (or seen as a celebration of life). The two trees not yet bearing leaves and fruit, much like the NFT itself. Nature is the silent witness to this great recycler season after season. And lastly, the setting sun taking its warmth and light, only to leave us in the dark of night — returning again in the morning as we are born again in the light.


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/7311a600-0b8a-4624-ab74-e4b06514e582/20260425-8570-z8-morden-silhouette-sunset-by-dougfriesen-bw.png)


Of course we saw this amazing scene. No clouds in the sky lost us the brilliant colours but brought back the clean minimalism of silhouettes. I first sent my friend up on the hill so that I could silhouette him taking a picture. Then he went back down behind me at my request, grabbed an artistic silhouette of my varied attempts to capture the Outsiders art.


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/5985b0e0-27cb-4186-bfb6-56cdd6a58859/STV09942-shot-by-stevehiebert-x.jpg)

Above: BTS silhouette of me trying different angles during my OUTSIDERS session. Image by Steve Hiebert (/stevehiebert on IG).


![Seize](https://d3lqz0a4bldqgf.cloudfront.net/drops/author_b0c4be70-59b2-4f39-a6fe-f03f90256f21/37137714-f5c8-445d-aade-51a257f17054/20260425-8564-z8-morden-silhouette-sunset-by-dougfriesen-w.png)

Above: I shot this image of Steve capturing his photographic art. I brought both trees in, gave more space to breathe with a wider focal length. These minimalist silhouettes are one of my favourite disciplines. I have always loved deep shadows and simplicity of distractions.

EVERYTHING MUST GO

Inscribed as a Bitcoin Ordinal to enhance its mortality in the face of its subject.


Back to last week again in Quebec City. On my walk to create some Outsiders content, I came across an access path I wanted to take onto the fortress wall of the city, but it was closed now... littered with garbage all around it. It was a bit disappointing at first, but then I remembered that every disappointment is just a challenge to make it beautiful or to tell story. So I got out my phone and flipped to my Ordinal NFT art with the intention.


What became as a simple photograph back in 2011 had now become a powerful message.


The Ordinal art is pure photography in high contrast monochrome. It is of a store front and old vehicle in London, UK, from when I was there in 2011. So there is vintage even in the image, per se. The juxtaposition within the art is prevalent. The store closing, signs and wording placed all over it. Everything Must Go. Even the car in the foreground is a reminder that was it new becomes old. And just like that photograph, this photograph enshrining the original is highlighting that as well. The path once kept and travelled was now closed and left in a stand of abandon. I am presenting it in black and white as the original art is and the overall aesthetics beg for it to extend the frame of the image art. I also tried to present this in a high contrast fashion that would accentuate the original.


In a world full of temporary promises, hold tight to that which outlasts. Memories are what you will cherish when you have nothing else. Those moments, smiles, adventures, lessons learned, and friendships made all contribute to what is priceless. And take photographs along the way. You are preserving history and your memories to rekindle in later years. 


Time is precious. You are precious.


In the end, everything must go.
